India withdraws cotton bales QCO after multiple extensions
content:
India’s Ministry of Textiles has withdrawn the Cotton Bales (Quality Control) Order, 2023, ending a BIS certification requirement that had never been implemented despite multiple extensions.
The measure faced strong opposition from the ginning industry, particularly MSMEs, over compliance costs and infrastructure challenges.
The withdrawal provides relief to domestic ginners.

title: Vietnam's customs revenue on track to meet annual target
content:
Vietnam’s budget revenue from foreign trade activities reached $8.17 billion in the first five months of 2026, equivalent to 47.7 per cent of the annual target and up by 16.9 per cent YoY. 
During January-May, exports rose by 19.5 per cent YoY to $215.66 billion, while imports surged by 30.8 per cent YoY to $229.46 billion. 
Total trade turnover hit $445.12 billion, up by 25 per cent YoY.

title: Pakistan’s textile exports face cotton shortage and tax strain
content:
Pakistan’s textile exports remain sizeable, but profitability is under pressure from cotton import dependence, tax-related liquidity constraints and slowing apparel and fabric shipments. 
Q1 2026 apparel exports fell 5.6 per cent. 
The sector’s competitiveness increasingly depends on improving cash flow predictability and reducing procurement risks rather than expanding production capacity.

title: ICE cotton futures remain weak despite signs of stabilisation
content:
ICE cotton futures remained under pressure, with the July contract falling to its lowest settlement since April 1 as fund liquidation and a stronger US dollar weighed on sentiment.
Weak crude oil and grain markets added to the bearish tone, while traders focused on July contract rollovers ahead of First Notice Day.
Technical factors continue to dominate price direction ahead of the WASDE report.

title: Can thrifting save fashion’s future?
content:
World Environment Day may have passed, but one sustainability challenge remains: fashion. 
The industry contributes up to 10 per cent of global emissions, while fast fashion fuels relentless consumption and leaves 85 per cent of textiles discarded annually. 
As resale and second-hand fashion gain traction, the key question is whether reuse can reduce overconsumption or simply reshape it.

title: US textile, apparel imports down 12% in Jan-April; China hit hardest
content:
US textile and apparel imports fell 12.06 per cent year on year to $31.11 billion in January-April 2026, led by a sharp decline in shipments from China.
Vietnam remained the largest supplier and expanded its market share, while Cambodia also posted strong growth.
Apparel imports dropped 11.90 per cent, reflecting shifting sourcing strategies and weaker overall import demand.

title: Humana Apparels boosts capacity 15% with Coats Digital solution
content:
Bangladesh-based Humana Apparels has improved operational efficiency after implementing Coats Digital’s FastReactPlan solution. 
The outerwear manufacturer achieved a 15 per cent increase in capacity utilisation, an 8 per cent productivity gain and a 5 per cent improvement in on-time delivery performance. 
Real-time planning and synchronised production processes reduced idle time.
